reporting-org.narrative: Fundacja im. Kazimierza Pułaskiego (Casimir Pulaski Foundation)

description.narrative:
Through the analysis conducted by Casimir Pulaski Foundation, the Embassy and other British stakeholders will receive evidence-based and comprehensive insights into Poland’s energy security landscape, detailing the challenges and offering meaningful ways of engagement for British stakeholders with their Polish counterparts. The salience of energy security has grown significantly since Russia’s attack on Ukraine. Since then, the geopolitical landscape in Europe has continued to deteriorate, as illustrated by various hybrid attacks on critical infrastructure carried out by both state and non-state actors. Energy-related infrastructure across Europe, and particularly in the Baltic Sea Region, has been weaponised by adversaries of the European Union. The protection of critical infrastructure has therefore become a key international priority for Poland, as reflected in the country’s agenda during its EU Council Presidency and its current Presidency of the Council of the Baltic Sea States.
At the same time, energy security cannot be discussed without considering the impacts of climate-induced disasters. Sea storms, floods, heat waves, and droughts increase the likelihood of hostile actions, including sabotage and disinformation, taking place below the threshold of open conflict.
